questions.prompt: What URL does app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx map to?
questions.explanation: Folder nesting mirrors URL nesting, so app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx serves /dashboard/settings.

questions.prompt: What makes a folder inside app/ a visitable route?

options.text: Adding a page.tsx (or route.ts) file to it

questions.explanation: A folder becomes a public route only when it contains a page.tsx (for UI) or route.ts (for an API). A folder by itself is not reachable.

questions.prompt: What is the exact (lowercase) file name that renders a route's UI in the App Router?
questions.explanation: The reserved file is page.tsx (lowercase). index.tsx and Page.tsx do not work.

questions.prompt: Which of these are reserved file names in a route folder? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: layout, loading, and not-found are reserved. PostCard.tsx is a non-reserved name, so it is a colocated helper, not a route.

questions.prompt: Order these folders from the shortest URL to the longest URL they produce.
questions.explanation: These map to /, /shop, /shop/shoes, and /shop/shoes/running — each added folder adds one URL segment.

questions.prompt: Match each file path to the URL it produces.
questions.explanation: Folder nesting mirrors URL nesting, so each page.tsx serves the URL formed by its folder path.
